# SPD-057 — Auto-claim a session in a claim project when Eric's prompt names one of that project's tickets

## Brief
Eric's call (2026-09-14): in a project whose sessions mode is `claim` (BadTakes), a session that is given a ticket should become Spud without him typing /spud first.

What went wrong: three BadTakes sessions started with "Work on BAD-006" and one with "Start on BAD-020", none with /spud. Each stayed a plain session: the desktop app titled it from the first message ("BAD-006", "BAD-020 ticket"), the session ritual never ran (so no `BAD-nnn - <what>` title), and the work happened outside the ledger. The BAD-006 session opened and merged PR 336 and the BAD-020 session rebased and re-verified PRs 327 and 328, with no team, no report entries and both tickets still queued. Sessions that did start with /spud (BAD-002, BAD-004, BAD-008..019) set their titles and wrote the ledger.

Build:
1. A `UserPromptSubmit` hook, installed by `spud settings sync` and `spud project install|sync` alongside the existing hooks (a project's hook line carries `--project <key>` and fails open with no agent_id, like the others). In a session whose mode is `plain` (an unclaimed session in a `claim` project), when the prompt names the key of an existing ticket of that session's project, it claims the session exactly as `spud --as spud session claim` does and returns additional context that makes the session Spud: the /spud skill's instructions (read the home CLAUDE.md and spud.config.json in full, the precedence rule, run the session ritual from step 2, including setting the session title to `<KEY> - <what this session does>`) plus the claim card. It records a claim event saying the hook claimed it and on which key.
2. Matching: only the project's own prefix, the ledger's key shape (`BAD-` and three digits), and only keys that exist in the tickets table. BadTakes pull requests and TODO.md cite an older tracker's numbers (BAD-23 to BAD-36, two digits, overlapping); they must never claim. A key of another project, a declined ticket, a prompt in the home, an already-claimed session, a subagent, and a released session (Eric ran `session release`) do nothing. Decide and document whether a done ticket claims (recommend yes: Eric may be reopening it).
3. A `plain` session whose prompt names no ticket stays silent, as today.
4. Tests for each case above, including the old-tracker two-digit numbers, and the full suite green.
5. Update CLAUDE.md's In another project section (Spud's own file, Spud edits it after landing) — leave a note in the result of what it should say.

Read first: bin/spud_ledger.py cmd_session_claim, claim_card, unclaimed_session_project, session_mode and the SessionStart hook's project_session_context; ~/.claude/skills/spud/SKILL.md (installed by project install); CLAUDE.md sections Session ritual, Ledger v1 (the hooks), In another project.

## Size, persona and model decision
One engineer on opus: a new hook event in bin/spud plus settings sync and project sync, with tests; the claim logic already exists (cmd_session_claim, claim_card). A reviewer only if the hook's matching turns out subtle.
